HPO-ODS-TOOLCHAIN-02.title: EXPLICIT_LOCAL_COMPILER_EXECUTION
HPO-ODS-TOOLCHAIN-02.relationship_to_v1_0_1: REFINES HPO-ODS-TOOLCHAIN-01. Does not revoke it. TOOLCHAIN-01 established that a governed typecheck must fail closed without a local toolchain; TOOLCHAIN-02 establishes that proving the PACKAGE exists is not the same as proving the COMPILER THAT RAN was the local one.

measured_failure.statement: A genuine local node_modules/typescript package may exist while node_modules/.bin/tsc does not. In that state `pnpm run typecheck` can resolve an ambient/global tsc and return exit 0. Proving the TypeScript package EXISTS is therefore insufficient.

independently_reproduced_at_ods_m1d.fixture: A disposable directory containing node_modules/typescript/package.json declaring {"name":"typescript","version":"5.9.3"}, with node_modules/.bin/tsc ABSENT and node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc ABSENT — i.e. no local compiler present at all.
independently_reproduced_at_ods_m1d.actual_execution: `pnpm run typecheck` in that same directory exited 0, compiled by an ambient tsc.
independently_reproduced_at_ods_m1d.conclusion: The v1.0.1 guard reports a green prerequisite for a worktree with no local compiler whatsoever, and the composed step it guards then succeeds against a global compiler. Confirmed by direct reproduction at ODS-M1D, not accepted on report. This is the same fail-open-by-absence class as the defects remediated in ODS-05-RM1: the check does not fail, it silently is not the check it claims to be.

frozen_requirements: The governed typecheck MUST NOT rely on ambient PATH resolution for tsc.
The governed typecheck MUST execute the compiler explicitly from the repository-local TypeScript package.

Preferred authorized mechanism: resolve repository root + node_modules/typescript/package.json + node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc; validate package metadata name == "typescript"; and require the compiler entry file to exist.
Execute the local compiler explicitly using the current Node runtime with repository root as cwd, semantically equivalent to: <process.execPath> <repoRoot>/node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit.
Do NOT invoke bare `tsc`, `pnpm run typecheck`, or `pnpm exec tsc` as the governed compiler execution where their correctness depends on PATH or bin-shim resolution.

Successful output/evidence MUST make local compiler identity observable, at minimum through stable fields LOCAL_TYPESCRIPT_PACKAGE, LOCAL_TYPESCRIPT_VERSION and LOCAL_TYPESCRIPT_COMPILER, or equivalent.
If package metadata or the local compiler entry is missing, malformed or inconsistent: FAIL before typecheck.
Ambient/global tsc availability or success MUST be irrelevant to the outcome.
No dependency or lockfile change is authorized.

required_controls.condition: fake package metadata only, no compiler entry file
genuine local package + compiler present, .bin shim absent, global tsc available
required_controls.required_result: governed typecheck MUST execute the LOCAL compiler, never the global one

required_controls.condition: global tsc returns 0 but local compiler unavailable

required_controls.required_result: local compiler identified and executed successfully

HPO-ODS-TOOLCHAIN-02.implementation_note_measured_at_ods_m1d: In this repository at the base commit, node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc and node_modules/typescript/bin/tsserver both exist and the package declares name "typescript", version "5.9.3" — so the preferred mechanism is materially available here and TC2-P is reachable without any dependency change.

HPO-ODS-POSTSTATE-01.title: PROTECTED_AUTHORITY_PASSTHROUGH
HPO-ODS-POSTSTATE-01.closes: W2-GAP-1 at the standard poststate layer

measured_state.statement: ods:scope correctly accepts --protected-authority HPO-ODS-W2-01, but ods:poststate cannot express or forward that authority, so the standard governed poststate workflow cannot close an authorized Wave 2 migration task.
measured_state.verified_at_ods_m1d: grep of scripts/ods-poststate.ts finds no occurrence of --protected-authority or protectedAuthority; scripts/ods-scope.ts implements it. Confirmed by direct inspection, not assumed.

frozen_requirements: ods:poststate SHALL accept --protected-authority <authority-id>.
The value is caller-supplied only as an authority IDENTIFIER.
ods:poststate MUST NOT interpret or expand the grant itself.
It SHALL forward the exact identifier only to its composed ods:scope step.
ods:scope remains the SOLE grant adjudicator for authority validity, branch binding, protected-pattern binding, concrete path, and ordinary task --allow.
Missing operand or malformed protected-authority usage at the poststate level => USAGE ERROR, non-zero.
When no authority identifier is provided, preserve the current fail-closed protected-path behavior.
Normal task --allow remains mandatory.
This passthrough MUST NOT make protected authorization available to any other poststate sub-gate.

required_controls.condition: migration path + ordinary allow but no protected authority
correct authority but ungranted protected sibling
correct authority but missing normal task allow
correct branch + HPO-ODS-W2-01 + granted migration/journal path + normal task allow
required_controls.required_result: ods:scope PASS inside ods:poststate; poststate may PASS if every other requested gate also passes

HPO-ODS-C4-CASE-01.title: CANONICAL_PROTECTED_PATH_CASING
HPO-ODS-C4-CASE-01.predates: This behavior predates v1.0.1; it is recorded here as a now-known C4 protection gap, not as a v1.0.1 regression.

measured_state.statement: A Git path such as DB/migrations/craft.sql can avoid the lower-case db/migrations/** protected classifier on a case-sensitive host.

independently_reproduced_at_ods_m1d.method: Called matchesAnyPattern(path, DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERNS) directly against the live implementation.
independently_reproduced_at_ods_m1d.conclusion: The bypass is real and is NOT limited to db/migrations/**: db/baseline/** — a surface no authority grants — is equally bypassable by case variant. This directly supports frozen requirement 7 below.

frozen_requirements: Protected-surface security classification MUST NOT be bypassable by case variants.
For security classification ONLY, detect case-insensitive equivalence to every protected surface.
The canonical repository casing remains the casing already declared by the protected patterns.
A concrete path that is case-insensitively within a protected surface but does not use canonical protected-surface casing is NON_CANONICAL_PROTECTED_PATH and MUST FAIL.
A non-canonical protected path MUST NOT become authorized even under a valid protected authority.
Do NOT solve this by lowercasing changed paths and then granting them. Detection may be case-insensitive; AUTHORIZATION remains bound to canonical concrete paths.
This decision applies to EVERY DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATTERN, not only db/migrations/**.
Git-standard "/" path semantics remain controlling. Do not invent Windows "\" repository paths.

required_controls.condition: canonical db/migrations/file.sql + valid HPO-ODS-W2-01 + ordinary allow

HPO-ODS-C4-CASE-01.fixture_note: If the host filesystem cannot physically materialize a case-variant path, exercise classification through a deterministic unit fixture and, where possible, Git-index or disposable-repository evidence.

cli_hygiene_authorization.requirement: A trailing --protected-authority with no operand MUST return a usage error rather than silently becoming NONE. Applies to both ods:scope and, once it supports the flag, ods:poststate.
cli_hygiene_authorization.not_a_new_capability: This authorizes no new authorization capability. It aligns --protected-authority with the trailing-operand rejection already applied to ods:prestate's value flags in ODS-05-RM1.
cli_hygiene_authorization.independently_reproduced_at_ods_m1d: `pnpm run ods:scope -- --base <sha> --allow x --protected-authority` (trailing, no operand) printed PROTECTED_AUTHORITY=NONE, ODS_SCOPE=PASS and exited 0. Same fail-open-by-absence shape as the ODS-05 prestate defect: the malformed flag is silently not applied rather than refused.
cli_hygiene_authorization.duplicate_flags: OUT OF SCOPE for this remediation unless implementation discovers a safety defect, in which case it must be reported rather than silently fixed.
